extracted.intended_audience: CIPR members and public relations / communications professionals (UK and international)
extracted.subtask_description: An organisational news/archive page listing CIPR press releases and announcements about awards, appointments, membership, surveys, policy papers, and professional standards. Useful for understanding institutional requirements and evaluation language used by the Chartered Institute of Public Relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence Awards evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognising the creativity, value, and impact of the UK's public relations and communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CIPR publishes a shortlist for its annual Excellence Awards, which evaluate submissions on creativity, value and impact. (Context: announcement of the shortlist for the 2026 Excellence Awards.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual CPD requirement — compulsory EDI and ethics points
rubrics_metrics.description: From 2026–2027, members that engage in the Institute’s CPD cycle will be required to log a minimum of five Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) points as part of their annual professional development; this sits alongside the existing ethics requirement within the 60-point annual CPD framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members' CPD cycles will only be marked as complete once both the EDI and ethics components are fulfilled. Over 80 free EDI activities are listed on the CIPR’s CPD database; members may also log bespoke or external EDI learning as a custom activity. The change was recommended by the EDI Committee and approved by Council and Board. MyCPD dashboard will track progress against the new requirement in the same way it does for ethics points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chartered Practitioner assessment standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates undertook a series of rigorous one-day assessments, demonstrating their expertise and knowledge of public relations practice across strategy, ethics, and leadership; those who successfully met the assessment criteria have been awarded PR's highest badge of professionalism (Chartered PR Practitioner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assessments are presented as rigorous, one-day examinations and cover strategy, ethics and leadership. The press item lists successful candidates across multiple jurisdictions (Belgium, UK, UAE and beyond) and notes this recognition brings the total number of Chartered Practitioners to a specified figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair of Examiners role: maintaining qualification standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair of Examiners is responsible for maintaining standards across the different CIPR qualifications delivered in the UK and overseas by CIPR Accredited Teaching Centres (ATCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chair has a strategic advisory role to ensure that CIPR Awarding Body assessment processes and course regulations are fit for purpose, including responsibility for developing assessment processes, course regulation and policy to ensure alignment with best practice in the area of Awarding Body services. (Context: appointment of Professor Susan Kinnear to the role for an initial three-year term.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate Affiliate membership expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate Affiliate members are described as being committed to the continued professional development of their PR and communications teams and upholding the highest ethical and professional standards in their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement lists recent corporate affiliates (NHS trusts, government departments, agencies, consultancies, etc.) and frames membership as a commitment to CPD and ethical/professional standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the Profession survey scope and benchmarking purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The State of the Profession survey captures practitioner perspectives on the health of the profession including skills and training needs, salaries, the reputation of PR, and how practitioners are responding to developments in artificial intelligence and the global news agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Now in its fourteenth year, the survey is used to benchmark standards, guide CIPR's policy agenda, and make representations to business, partners and legislators. The survey is open to all, takes approximately 10 minutes to complete, and offers entry into a prize draw for a £100 gift card upon completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for nominations to CIPR leadership positions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institute is inviting nominations for President-Elect, Board of Directors, and Council; members are invited generally, and for Board positions non-members may also be invited to stand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural eligibility note embedded in the nominations announcement — it signals who may be considered for governance roles (members for most roles; Board positions open to non-members as well) and implies the Institute’s selection process includes external recruitment to shape direction.
